D005-D015_h001.question_both:
It’s hard to explain, but for the last couple of months I’ve felt like something’s really off with me.

I drive the city bus on the early shift, and lately I’ve had this strong sense that I’m… meant for more than this. Not just in a “daydreaming” way. It feels almost like I’ve been chosen for some special role, like I’m supposed to be noticed by important people, maybe even involved in some bigger plan. I catch myself thinking that the cameras on the bus or the traffic lights are somehow tracking me because I’m important, like they’re watching to see what I’ll do.

Around the same time, I started smelling things that no one else seems to notice. Sometimes it’s this strong burning or chemical smell, other times like rotten food, even when the bus is clean and the passengers say they don’t smell anything. It can happen at home too, when my wife doesn’t notice anything.

I’ve been more down and tired than usual, not enjoying stuff I used to, but I’m not sure if that’s because of all this or something else. I just know this has been going on for about two months and it’s really worrying me.
D005-D015_h001.question_a:
For the past couple of months, I’ve been convinced I’m not just some regular bus driver. I keep feeling like I’ve been chosen for something big, like I’m supposed to guide people, not just on the route, but in their lives. It sounds odd even saying it out loud, but it feels real, like I have this special purpose or power that other people don’t see yet.

Around the same time, I started noticing strange smells, like burning rubber or a strong chemical odor, especially when I’m alone in the bus or at home in the living room. My wife and coworkers don’t smell anything, but it’s so vivid to me that I’ll get up and check the engine or the stove. It happens on and off throughout the day, every day.

I did feel really low for a week or so recently—tired, guilty about not being a good husband, not enjoying anything—but that kind of came and went. These beliefs about being chosen and the weird smells have just kept going steadily for about two months, no matter how my mood is.
D005-D015_h001.question_b:
I’ve been feeling really low for a long time now… I’d say at least six months. It’s gotten worse over the last couple of months. I drag myself out of bed at 4 a.m. for my bus route, but I’m exhausted before I even start. Nothing feels enjoyable anymore—not driving, not watching the game, not even spending time with my wife or grandkids. I feel guilty all the time, like I’ve failed my family and don’t deserve them.

About two months ago, on top of feeling so down, I started getting these strange ideas. I became convinced I had some kind of special calling, like I’d been chosen to “save” people on my route, that I had powers to protect them from accidents. It sounds odd even as I say it, but it feels real in the moment.

Around the same time, I began smelling smoke or rotting meat when no one else could smell anything—on the bus, at home, even in bed. Those smells and those beliefs only happen when I’m in this really dark mood; when my mood lifts a bit for a day or two, that stuff fades too.

Lately I keep getting this feeling that people are watching me, like there are cameras hidden in the apartment or the neighbors are listening in through the walls. When I’m at work, I catch myself wondering if my patients are actually there to spy on me or report on me to someone. I know that sounds irrational, and part of me can tell it doesn’t really make sense, but the feeling doesn’t go away.

Around the same time, my mood dropped a lot. I’m exhausted all the time, I cry for no clear reason, and I’ve lost interest in things I used to enjoy, even just relaxing with my husband. It’s like I’m moving through molasses.

Another weird thing is that I sometimes suddenly taste metal or something rotten in my mouth, even when I haven’t eaten anything. It makes me nauseous and more on edge. All of this together is making it really hard to focus at work and at home.
D005-D015_h002.question_a:

At work, I began getting this strong feeling that people were watching me, like my patients or even the front desk staff were secretly recording me or talking about me to some group online. I know it sounds odd, but I feel like someone is tracking what I do, maybe through the cameras in the office or even my phone. I check corners or look over my shoulder a lot, even at home.

Around the same time, I started getting these strange taste sensations. I’ll be cleaning someone’s teeth or just drinking water, and suddenly I taste this bitter, metallic, almost chemical flavor in my mouth, like poison or something rotten, even though there’s nothing there. It makes me scared to eat sometimes.

I have been feeling down and low-energy on and off, especially the past few weeks—some mornings I don’t want to get out of bed and I feel like a failure as a wife and at my job. But even on days when my mood is okay or a bit better, the sense of being watched and those weird tastes don’t stop. They’ve been there pretty much constantly for these two months.

I know it sounds odd, but it feels so real. At home, sometimes I suddenly get this strong taste in my mouth, like metal or chemicals, when I’m just sitting there and not eating anything. These things only happen when I’m in this really low, hopeless state. Before this depressive slump, I never experienced anything like that.

It’s been about three months now that things have really felt off. It started with this feeling that something is wrong inside my body. I’m convinced there’s some kind of rot or worms in my stomach or my blood, even though the village doctor keeps saying my tests look fine. I can almost feel it crawling sometimes, and I can’t shake the thought that my insides are being eaten away.

Around the same time, I began hearing this voice, usually in the evenings after work, sometimes even out in the fields when I’m alone with the crops. It’s not like someone calling from far away; it’s right by my ear, talking about how my body is broken, how I’m useless. No one else hears it. It’s not all the time, but it keeps coming back.

My wife says I don’t talk like I used to. I’ll start telling her about the weather, then suddenly I’m talking about the worms, then about the price of fertilizer, and I lose track of what I was saying. I’ve pulled back a lot from neighbors, stopped going to gatherings. I just don’t feel like being around anyone, and I mostly keep to myself on the farm or in the house.

Around the same time, I began hearing voices out in the fields and in the house, usually more than one, talking about me. They say things like “he’s useless,” “he’s poisoned,” sometimes they argue with each other, but no one else hears them. They come whether I’m sad or not, even when I’m just trying to fix the tractor or count the sacks of grain.

I’ve pulled back from folks. I don’t go to the tea stall, I avoid neighbors, even my own brothers. My wife says I just sit and stare.
